refinements.baseline: The pinned primary badge path (assembleBadgeV1 in the provider's componentAssembly) seeds the badge from its accepted outer bright component, the white ribbon, and owns the largest contained dark component as a member; the plate-base order exists only in the provider's dark-plate recovery path, whose assemblies the object-graph path marks failed. The toolkit seam receives the outcome as a finished px array with white/black counts; the fused set's component structure does not cross the seam.
refinements.declaredBy: Sam, 2026-10-17: there is a literal step fusing the Black and White PxSets into the full sprite; per sprite, assembly starts from the more reliable base PxSet and fuses the rest onto it; for a badge the base is the inner plate, because the outer ribbon is bright and can merge into other bright sprites' pixels (a basket glyph) and stop being family, while the plate body is enclosed and cannot merge
refinements.delta: Each Badge Part is re-assembled plate-first through the phase-1 assembly shape (ports/early/assembly.mjs): the plate component set is the declared base; the white frame/ribbon component and one component per digit (the union of that digit's bright glyph components, assigned by digit-bbox enclosure) are fused onto it. The fused set is order-independent, so the delta is structural, not pixel-changing: the Part crosses the seam as named components with roles instead of a flat array, carries its anchor (the plate centroid, with the fused-set centroid and their delta recorded, flagged past 2 px), carries digit counters as digit-owned sub-structure under the accepted ownership-by-enclosure counter rule (they stay outside the fused set, as in px.badges, and reconcile at the digit layer), and accounts ownership against its Part bbox with the residue named per badge. The base board and px.badges are never written; the assembly lives only on the branch and in its artifact.
refinements.enforcement: Toolkit layer only: ports/early/s1BadgeAssembly.mjs (the assembly Calculation and the independent witness) plus the branch and guarantee in fg/s1/fg.s1.pxBadges.assembly.fg.mjs (run by ports/early/runEarly.mjs through the fg registry), gated by lane s1-badge-assembly through ports/run-stages.mjs. The pinned provider is untouched, and with the lane OFF the stage reproduces the pinned baseline emissions exactly.
refinements.specimenExpectation: On the golden specimen (Dash IMG_5641.jpg) the assembly reproduces all 18 badges exactly (fused union 37,002 px; white 11,565; black 25,437), attributes the same 10 counter components (293 px) to the same digits as fg.s1.pxDigits.materialize, and reconciles owned-with-counters to 37,295 px, with S0, S2 and S3 emissions untouched. This expectation is enforced as exact gates in the wiring (the guarantee certifies reproduction, not a recorded delta), because plate-first assembly must not change a single pixel; any differing badge is reported with its differing pixel count.

responsibility: Recover badge objects and their numeral cardinality from canonical course pixels.
